title: Tighten structural C# emitter correctness gates
description:
The current C# emitter is back on the structural path, but several permissive success paths can still hide unsupported Java constructs. Fix these before expanding emitter coverage.

Context:
- vibeformer/src/vibeformer/emit/csharp.clj now dispatches primarily from Datomic node/ref/type facts rather than regex over source text. Keep that direction.
- clojure -T:build test and manual dotnet build currently pass for java-word-count, but the emitter still has correctness gaps that could make coverage/provenance look greener than the transformer really is.

Scope:
- Replace the generic method-call success fallback in emit-method-call with a guarded path: only emit a normal call when the ref is resolved and known to be project-local or otherwise explicitly supported. Unknown/unresolved external calls must produce unsupported diagnostics and failed rule applications.
- Make field/member special cases such as length structural: array length should be emitted only when type/ref facts prove the target is an array or supported length-bearing construct, not merely because the field name is length.
- Register explicit transform rules for special API mappings currently used by the emitter, including Pattern.compile -> Regex, String.trim, String.isEmpty, Pattern.split, PrintStream.println, System.exit, Path.of, and Files.readString, so provenance rule metadata is not nil.
- Ensure provenance/rule applications for these special mappings resolve to real rule catalog entries with rule id, version, status, source language, and input selector.
- Keep source text out of rule dispatch. Source text may appear only as debug/evidence context if needed, not as the selector for transformations.
- Review the sample-runner coverage behavior: emission should not proceed silently after a non-green coverage gate unless an explicit allow mode is present and recorded.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unknown or unresolved method calls in emitted statement/expression bodies produce structured diagnostics rather than successful generated calls.
- length emission is backed by structural type/ref facts or reports unsupported.
- All special Java API mapping rule ids emitted by csharp.clj are registered in the transform rule catalog and show non-nil metadata in provenance.
- Tests cover at least one unsupported method call and one unsupported/ambiguous length-like field access.
- Tests assert special API provenance contains real rule metadata.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: Add transform rule registry and coverage gates

Scope:

- Produce actionable coverage failures with source file, source span, node/feature kind, and missing/ambiguous rule information.
- Support an explicit stub/unsupported mode boundary without silently emitting nonsense.

Out of scope:
- Full C# emitter implementation.
- Compiler diagnostic ingestion.
- Advanced transform behavior beyond metadata and coverage gating.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rule metadata can be registered and queried by source language and node/feature kind.
- Coverage gates fail clearly for missing or ambiguous rules.
- Coverage gates pass when representative source facts are fully covered or explicitly stubbed.
- Tests cover implemented, unsupported, missing, and ambiguous rule cases.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Canonicalize Java method-call source nodes
description:
The Java Spoon ingester currently creates method-call source nodes through two paths: structural expression-facts under the real expression/statement parent, and executable-invocation-facts as flat nodes directly under the executable. These can represent the same source invocation with different :node/id values, which can inflate inventory, make coverage green for nodes the emitter never traverses, and split provenance/diagnostics across non-canonical source nodes.

Scope:
- Make structural expression nodes the canonical representation for Java method calls.
- Remove or refactor executable-invocation-facts so it does not create a second :java.node/method-call node for the same source construct.
- Preserve method-call refs, owner/return type facts, and invocation feature facts by attaching them to the canonical structural method-call node.
- Ensure source spans, roles, ordinals, and parent relationships remain deterministic.
- Update coverage/inventory tests so each source invocation appears once as a node while refs/features remain queryable.
- Verify emitter provenance and rule applications refer to the same canonical method-call node that inventory/coverage see.

Acceptance criteria:
- A Java fixture with nested/statement method calls produces exactly one :java.node/method-call node per source invocation.
- Method-call refs are attached to the canonical structural node.
- Reflection/stream invocation feature facts, where applicable, attach to the canonical structural node or its intended containing source node without duplicate invocation nodes.
- Existing C# emitter tests still pass.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

Scope:

Non-goals / constraints:
- Do not dispatch transform rules by regex over :node/source-text. Source text may be retained as evidence/debug context, but it must not select the rule or be the primary conversion input.
- Do not parse generated C# to infer what happened. Transform output should carry diagnostics/provenance metadata as it is emitted.
- Do not mark broad expression or statement kinds implemented unless their structural emitter handles the relevant node shape and reports unsupported subcases.
- Do not patch generated C# directly; generated output remains disposable.

Acceptance criteria:

- Remaining unsupported expressions are reported with source path, span, node kind, and rule context.
- Unit or golden tests cover the emitted statement/expression subset.

title: Datomic schema for files, nodes, declarations, types, refs, features
description:
**Implementation Plan**

Build this as a small schema foundation, not as extractor work yet.

1. Add a schema namespace:
   - Create `src/vibeformer/datomic/schema.clj`.
   - Expose `schema` or `all` as pure Datomic tx-data.
   - Optional helper: `install! [conn]` wrapping `(d/transact conn {:tx-data all})`.
   - Keep no new dependencies.

2. Define stable identity conventions:
   - Add minimal `:project/id` because `:file/project` already appears in the model docs.
   - Use `:file/id` as the file identity, not only `:file/path`, so multiple projects can contain the same relative path.
   - Keep `:file/path` indexed/queryable.
   - Use unique identity attrs for `:node/id`, `:decl/id`, `:type/id`, `:ref/id`, and `:feature/id`.

3. Implement schema groups:
   - Project/file attrs: project id/name/root, file id/path/lang/hash/project/package.
   - Node attrs: id/lang/kind/name/file/parent/ordinal/source span/source hash.
   - Declaration attrs: id/lang/kind/name/qualified-name/source-node/return-type/type/modifiers.
   - Type attrs: id/lang/name/nullable flag, plus ordered type-argument support via small arg entities if needed.
   - Reference attrs: id/kind/from-node/to-decl/to-type/name/owner-type/resolved flag/reason.
   - Feature attrs: id/lang/kind/node/status/severity.

4. Refactor the existing Datomic smoke test:
   - Remove the inline `datomic-smoke-schema` from `test/vibeformer/vibeformer_test.clj`.
   - Use the new schema namespace in the existing Datomic Local test.
   - Transact a richer fixture covering file, node, declaration, type, resolved ref, unresolved ref, and feature.
   - Assert the key joins needed by the next steps:
     - file -> node -> declaration
     - declaration -> return/type
     - ref -> source node -> optional target declaration/type
     - feature inventory counts by kind/status
     - unsupported features by file

5. Add focused schema tests:
   - New test namespace is probably cleaner: `test/vibeformer/datomic/schema_test.clj`.
   - Verify the schema transacts into a fresh Datomic Local in-memory DB.
   - Verify lookup refs work for every unique identity attr.
   - Verify re-transacting an entity by identity updates facts rather than duplicating logical records.
   - Verify ordered fields that matter, especially node ordinal and any type-arg ordinal approach.

6. Update docs:
   - Update `doc/datomic-model.md` to reflect any concrete schema decisions, especially `:file/id` and ordered type argument representation if used.
   - Keep README unchanged unless a new quick-start command is added, which is unlikely.

7. Validation:
   - Run `clojure -T:build test`.
   - Run `git diff --check`.
   - Run `br sync --flush-only` before committing, per repo workflow.

**Out Of Scope**

No extractor changes, no Spoon/Kotlin fact emission, no feature inventory CLI, no transform/emitter work, and no durable Datomic storage setup. This step only creates the canonical schema and proves it supports the fact graph shape the next implementation steps will need.

**Epic Acceptance Criteria**

The epic is done when Vibeformer has a reusable Datomic schema namespace, tests transact and query a representative file/node/decl/type/ref/feature graph in Datomic Local, the old inline smoke schema is gone, docs match the implemented schema, and `clojure -T:build test` passes.

Acceptance criteria:
- A developer can run the sample command with an explicit unsupported/stub allow option.
- stages.edn records the allow mode when used.
- The default strict mode still fails on unsupported coverage for a fixture that has no allow option.
- Tests cover option propagation from build/CLI layer where practical.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.
